GROUP THEORY AND GENERALIZATIONS

1153-20-351
Emily R Stark* (stark@math.utah.edu) and Daniel J Woodhouse
(daniel.woodhouse@mail.mcgill.edu). Action rigidity for free products of hyperbolic
manifold groups.
The relationship between the large-scale geometry of a group and its algebraic structure can be studied via three
notions: a group’s quasi-isometry class, a group’s abstract commensurability class, and geometric actions of a
group on proper geodesic metric spaces. A common model geometry for groups G and G’ is a proper geodesic
metric space on which G and G’ act geometrically. A group G is action rigid if every group G’ that has a common
model geometry with G is abstractly commensurable to G. For example, a closed hyperbolic n-manifold group
is not action rigid for all n at least three. We show that free products of closed hyperbolic manifold groups are
action rigid. Consequently, we obtain the ﬁrst examples of Gromov hyperbolic groups that are quasi-isometric
but do not virtually have a common model geometry. This is joint work with Daniel Woodhouse.
(Received
September 01, 2019)
1153-20-379
Larissa V. Sbitneva* (larissa@uaem.mx), Av. Universidad 1001, Col. Chamilpa, 62209
Cuernavaca, Morelos, Mexico. On the Lie’s third inverse theorem for smooth right Bol
loops with some additional properties.
The left Bol loops with the automorphic inverse property are known as left Bruck loops in the theory of nonas-
sociative algebraic structures, as well, the corresponding structures have been found in applications to Special
Relativity, as the gyrogroups (here the gyrocommutative property represents an explicit form of the Bruck iden-
tity). The smooth left Bol loops satisfying the Bruck identity play important role in the theory of symmetric
spaces of E. Cartan being geodesic loops of the aﬃne connection for such spaces. In our presentation we deal,
in particular, with the dual construction of smooth right Bruck loops. Being smooth right Bol loops they admit
the application of the general theory of Smooth Bol loops-Bol algebas. Analyzing the integrability conditions for
the diﬀerential equations of an arbitrary smooth right Bol loop we obtain the matrix form of the corresponding
diﬀerential equations on the structure functions. For the case of smooth right Bruck loops and due to another
speciﬁcation of the characteristic conditions on the Bol Algebra, it is shown how the explicit expression for the
structure functions can be presented in the form of series of hyperbolic functions. Then, an analog of the Lie’s
third inverse theorem for Bol algebras can be applied.
(Received September 02, 2019)
1153-20-383
Julianne Rainbolt*, julianne.rainbolt@slu.edu. A Supercharacter Theory Based on the
Degrees of Irreducible Characters.
The talk will begin with an introduction to Supercharacter Theory as deﬁned by P. Diaconis and I.M. Isaacs
(2007). A possible Supercharacter Theory based on the degrees of the irreducible characters of a ﬁnite group
will then be discussed. A proof that this Supercharacter Theory applies for certain families of ﬁnite groups but
does not apply for other families will be exhibited.
(Received September 02, 2019)
1153-20-399
Shawn T Burkett* (sburket1@kent.edu). A Jordan–H¨older type theorem for
supercharacter theories.
The Jordan–H¨older Theorem is a general term given to a collection of theorems about maximal chains in suitably
nice lattices. For example, the well-known Jordan–H¨older type theorem for chief series of ﬁnite groups has been
rather useful in studying the structure of ﬁnite groups. In this paper, we present a Jordan–H¨older type theorem
for supercharacter theories of ﬁnite groups, which generalizes the one for chief series of ﬁnite groups.
(Received
September 02, 2019)

Jay Taylor* (jayt@usc.edu), Department of Mathematics, 3620 South Vermont Avenue,
KAP 104, Los Angeles, CA 90089-2532, and Olivier Dudas and Olivier Brunat.
Unitriangular Shape of Decomposition Matrices of Unipotent Blocks.
Assume G is a ﬁnite reductive group deﬁned over a ﬁnite ﬁeld of characteristic p and assume r is a prime diﬀerent
from p. A long standing conjecture of Geck–Hiß states that the r-decomposition matrix of any unipotent block
of a ﬁnite reductive group should have a natural unitriangular shape, under some mild restrictions on p and r.
In this talk we present some recent progress regarding this conjecture.
(Received September 02, 2019)

Jamison Blair Barsotti* (jbbarsotti@wm.edu), Department of Mathematics, William &

Burnside ring.
